## 9. Stabilizers

**Proposition 9.** Let (C,gamma,Gamma) be a geometric point of Z_ev, so Gamma=(p_1,...,p_6) is an ordered tuple of pairwise distinct points with O_C(Gamma) iso L. (a) If the images gamma(p_i) take at least three distinct values and at least one p_i is unramified for gamma, then Aut(C,gamma,Gamma)=1. (b) Aut(C,gamma,Gamma)->Aut(C,Gamma) is an isomorphism. (c) On every geometric fibre the set of reduced Gamma in |L_b| for which the hypothesis of (a) fails is contained in a proper closed subset of |L_b| iso P^2; hence the trivial-stabilizer locus is a dense open subset of every geometric fibre of Z_ev->B.

*Proof.* (a) An element sigma of Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) is an automorphism of C with gamma o sigma = sigma-bar o gamma for a unique sigma-bar in Aut(P^1) (unique since gamma is surjective), and sigma(p_i)=p_i for all i. Then sigma-bar fixes each gamma(p_i); an element of PGL_2 fixing three distinct points is the identity, so sigma-bar=id and sigma lies in Aut(C/P^1). Let U be the nonempty open locus over which gamma is etale; gamma^{-1}(U) is a dense open of the irreducible C, hence connected, and gamma^{-1}(U)->U is finite etale of degree 4. The fixed locus of the U-automorphism sigma on this cover is open and closed and by hypothesis contains a point p_i; connectedness gives sigma=id on gamma^{-1}(U), hence sigma=id on C by density and separatedness.

(b) One inclusion is clear. Conversely let sigma be in Aut(C,Gamma), i.e. sigma(p_i)=p_i for all i. Then sigma^*O_C(Gamma) iso O_C(Gamma) and sigma^*omega_C iso omega_C, so sigma^*L iso L and hence sigma^*O_C(D) iso O_C(D) since D=K-L in Pic(C). By Proposition 3, h^0(D)=2, so |D| is the complete pencil defining gamma and sigma preserves it, inducing sigma-bar in PGL_2 with gamma o sigma = sigma-bar o gamma. Thus sigma lies in Aut(C,gamma,Gamma).

(c) *Unramified condition.* The ramification locus of gamma is a finite subset R of C. A reduced Gamma all of whose points lie in R is determined by a 6-element subset of R, so there are only finitely many such Gamma: a proper closed subset of the irreducible P^2.

*Three-distinct-images condition.* A reduced Gamma of degree 6 cannot have a single image, since a fibre of gamma has at most 4 points. Suppose Gamma has exactly two images y_1,y_2. Then Gamma is at most gamma^*(y_1)+gamma^*(y_2), so R_0:=gamma^*(y_1+y_2)-Gamma is effective of degree 2 with O(R_0) iso O(2D) tensor L^{-1}=O(3D) tensor omega^{-1}. If that h^0 is 0, no such Gamma exists. If it is 1, R_0 is unique, and any admissible pair {y_1,y_2} must contain gamma(supp R_0); the set of such pairs inside |O_{P^1}(2)|=P^2 is a point (if supp R_0 has two distinct gamma-images) or a line (if it has one), so the resulting set of Gamma has dimension at most 1. In all cases the locus of reduced Gamma with at most two distinct images lies in a closed subset of dimension at most 1, hence proper in P^2.

The union of the two exceptional loci is therefore a proper closed subset of |L_b|, and its preimage in the fibre of Z_ev is a proper closed subset whose complement is dense open. QED

Assume p is a base point. Then D+p is special (h^1=3-5+5=3>0). If |D+p| had a base point q then h^0(D+p-q)=3 with degree 4, and Clifford equality (2=4/2) with 4 not in {0,10} would force C hyperelliptic, a contradiction; so |D+p| is base-point-free. Then p_a(Z)=(5-1)(5-2)/2=6=g(C), and C->Z is the normalization, so the total delta-invariant vanishes and Z is smooth with C iso Z. Thus C is a smooth plane quintic, contradicting Lemma 4 (which applies to the given degree-four gamma). Hence |L| has no base point. QED

## 9. Stabilizers

**Proposition 9.** Let (C,gamma,Gamma) be a geometric point of Z_ev, so Gamma=(p_1,...,p_6) is an ordered tuple of pairwise distinct points with O_C(Gamma) iso L. (a) If the images gamma(p_i) take at least three distinct values and at least one p_i is unramified for gamma, then Aut(C,gamma,Gamma)=1. (b) Aut(C,gamma,Gamma)->Aut(C,Gamma) is an isomorphism. (c) On every geometric fibre the set of reduced Gamma in |L_b| for which the hypothesis of (a) fails is contained in a proper closed subset of |L_b| iso P^2; hence the trivial-stabilizer locus is a dense open subset of every geometric fibre of Z_ev->B.

*Proof.* (a) An element sigma of Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) is an automorphism of C with gamma o sigma = sigma-bar o gamma for a unique sigma-bar in Aut(P^1) (unique since gamma is surjective), and sigma(p_i)=p_i for all i. Then sigma-bar fixes each gamma(p_i); an element of PGL_2 fixing three distinct points is the identity, so sigma-bar=id and sigma lies in Aut(C/P^1). Let U be the nonempty open locus over which gamma is etale; gamma^{-1}(U) is a dense open of the irreducible C, hence connected, and gamma^{-1}(U)->U is finite etale of degree 4. The fixed locus of the U-automorphism sigma on this cover is open and closed and by hypothesis contains a point p_i; connectedness gives sigma=id on gamma^{-1}(U), hence sigma=id on C by density and separatedness.

(b) One inclusion is clear. Conversely let sigma be in Aut(C,Gamma), i.e. sigma(p_i)=p_i for all i. Then sigma^*O_C(Gamma) iso O_C(Gamma) and sigma^*omega_C iso omega_C, so sigma^*L iso L and hence sigma^*O_C(D) iso O_C(D) since D=K-L in Pic(C). By Proposition 3, h^0(D)=2, so |D| is the complete pencil defining gamma and sigma preserves it, inducing sigma-bar in PGL_2 with gamma o sigma = sigma-bar o gamma. Thus sigma lies in Aut(C,gamma,Gamma).

(c) *Unramified condition.* The ramification locus of gamma is a finite subset R of C. A reduced Gamma all of whose points lie in R is determined by a 6-element subset of R, so there are only finitely many such Gamma: a proper closed subset of the irreducible P^2.

*Three-distinct-images condition.* A reduced Gamma of degree 6 cannot have a single image, since a fibre of gamma has at most 4 points. Suppose Gamma has exactly two images y_1,y_2. Then Gamma is at most gamma^*(y_1)+gamma^*(y_2), so R_0:=gamma^*(y_1+y_2)-Gamma is effective of degree 2 with O(R_0) iso O(2D) tensor L^{-1}=O(3D) tensor omega^{-1}. Since C is not hyperelliptic (Lemma 2 with balancedness) and deg(O(3D) tensor omega^{-1})=2, we have h^0(O(3D) tensor omega^{-1})<=1, an h^0 of 2 being a g^1_2. If that h^0 is 0, no such Gamma exists. If it is 1, R_0 is unique, and any admissible pair {y_1,y_2} must contain gamma(supp R_0); the set of such pairs inside |O_{P^1}(2)|=P^2 is a point (if supp R_0 has two distinct gamma-images) or a line (if it has one), so the resulting set of Gamma has dimension at most 1. In all cases the locus of reduced Gamma with at most two distinct images lies in a closed subset of dimension at most 1, hence proper in P^2.

The union of the two exceptional loci is therefore a proper closed subset of |L_b|, and its preimage in the fibre of Z_ev is a proper closed subset whose complement is dense open. QED
